title: The Architecture of Mongolian Sentences: Head-Final SOV Word Order
primaryPurpose: Introduce the canonical Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) sentence topology of Modern Mongolian.
communicativeOutcome: Recognize that modifiers precede heads and the finite predicate anchors the absolute end of the clause.
readingObjective: Identify Subject, Object, and Verb in 5 color-coded simple sentence strips.
listeningObjective: Detect the finite verb dropping into sentence-final position with terminal cadence.
writingObjective: Arrange scrambled words into strictly grammatically correct SOV sequence.
spokenProductionObjective: Produce 3 simple subject-verb utterances without foreign SVO word order leakage.
pragmaticTarget: Establishing grammatical sentence architecture for all spoken interaction.
reviewReason: Bridge Pre-A1 script literacy into formal A1 clause architecture.
audioPurpose: Clear terminal falling intonation contours marking the end of SOV clauses.
successCriteria: Correctly order 5 out of 5 scrambled subject-verb clauses.
Identify the predicate slot in written sentences consistently and accurately.
masteryEvidence: Never places the verb between subject and object.
Correctly identifies that modifiers always precede their head nouns.

title: Formal Salutations by Time of Day: Өглөөний, Өдрийн, Оройн мэнд хүргэе
primaryPurpose: Expand time greetings into full formal performative sentences using 'хүргэе' (I convey).
communicativeOutcome: Formally convey time-based greetings ('Өглөөний мэнд хүргэе', 'Танд өдрийн мэнд хүргэе') in professional and polite contexts.
readingObjective: Read formal corporate emails and official conference greeting slides.
listeningObjective: Identify formal time greetings delivered in television and radio broadcast openings.
writingObjective: Write out 'Танд өглөөний мэнд хүргэе' correctly in Cyrillic.
spokenProductionObjective: Deliver formal greetings with respectful posture and warm vocal projection.
pragmaticTarget: Opening formal business meetings and professional correspondence respectfully.
reviewReason: Elevate Pre-A1 informal time greetings into complete formal grammatical sentences.
audioPurpose: Professional radio announcer voice greetings recorded at natural tempo.
successCriteria: Select 'хүргэе' as sentence-final performative verb in formal salutations.
Appropriately use 'Танд' (to you, polite) when greeting superiors.
masteryEvidence: Addresses office colleagues with 'Танд өглөөний мэнд хүргэе' smoothly.
Maintains proper long vowel duration on 'хүргэе'.

title: Inquiring After Peace and Wellbeing: Амар байна уу? & Мэнд ээ
primaryPurpose: Introduce traditional and formal inquiries after peace ('Амар байна уу?') and their customary ceremonial responses.

listeningObjective: Recognize traditional greeting formulas spoken during Tsagaan Sar (Lunar New Year) and rural hospitality.
writingObjective: Transcribe the paired greeting-response exchange accurately.
spokenProductionObjective: Execute traditional inquiry 'Та амар байна уу?' with respectful vocal inflection.
pragmaticTarget: Greeting elders and hosts when visiting a traditional Mongolian ger home.
reviewReason: Provide the culturally deep counterpart to standard urban 'Сайн байна уу?'.
audioPurpose: Authentic rural elder dialogues with respectful conversational cadence.
successCriteria: Pair 'Та амар байна уу?' with 'Амархан сайн байна уу?' in accurately and reliably of elder scenarios.
Articulate 'амар' with proper short vowels without elongation.
masteryEvidence: Never greets an elder with casual 'Сайн уу'.
Demonstrates awareness of traditional body language (sleeves down, hands extended).

title: The Nominative Personal Pronoun Paradigm: Би, Чи, Та, Тэр, Бид, Та нар, Тэд
primaryPurpose: Introduce the complete paradigm of nominative personal pronouns across singular and plural persons.
communicativeOutcome: Identify and use personal pronouns to refer to self, interlocutor, and third parties in basic clauses.

title: Direct Address Protocols: The Crucial Contrast Between Чи (Informal) and Та (Polite)
primaryPurpose: Analyze the social and ethical rules governing the choice between intimate 'Чи' and deferential 'Та'.
communicativeOutcome: Avoid social offense by strictly addressing elders, teachers, strangers, and officials with 'Та'.

listeningObjective: Detect tone of deference when native speakers address others using 'Та'.

spokenProductionObjective: Address an elder actor with 'Та' and a child actor with 'Чи' in interactive simulations.
pragmaticTarget: Upholding Mongolian cultural norms of age deference and professional respect.
reviewReason: Deepen pronoun paradigm with sociolinguistic address rules.
audioPurpose: Contrasting conversational audio vignettes highlighting social status.
successCriteria: Select 'Та' in accurately and reliably of elder, professional, and stranger scenarios.
Reserve 'Чи' strictly for intimate friends, close peers, and younger children.
masteryEvidence: Never addresses an instructor or stranger as 'Чи'.
Explains that addressing an elder as 'Чи' is considered a serious breach of etiquette.

title: Plural Pronouns and Collective Address: Та нар, Бид нар, Тэд нар
primaryPurpose: Introduce the collective plural marker 'нар' used with human personal pronouns.
communicativeOutcome: Address groups of people politely ('Та нар сайн байна уу?') and refer to collective bodies ('Бид нар оюутнууд').

pragmaticTarget: Addressing meetings, classrooms, and family gatherings effectively.
reviewReason: Expand personal pronouns to group dynamics and classroom speech.
audioPurpose: Teacher addressing a classroom of students.
successCriteria: Distinguish between singular polite 'Та' and plural 'Та нар' in 10 listening items.
Accurately use 'Бид нар' when representing a group.
masteryEvidence: Addresses a committee with 'Та бүхэн' or 'Та нар' correctly.
Spells 'нар' with correct short 'а' vowel.

audioPurpose: Authentic zero-copula statement recordings with pitch drop on final noun.
successCriteria: Form 5 zero-copula sentences without inserting an auxiliary verb.
Identify unmarked nominative subject and predicate nominal arguments correctly.
masteryEvidence: Never says 'Би байна багш' for identity statements.
Understands that 'Би багш' is a complete, grammatically perfect Mongolian sentence.

title: Stating Nationality & Geographic Origin: Монгол, Америк, Солонгос, Япон
primaryPurpose: Introduce major country and nationality nouns and combine them with zero-copula predication.
